utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If the usher would lower the shutters and the witness can be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may while that's being done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: There is a -- there was one document that I showed the witness on Friday which I neglected to move into evidence. And I would ask -- I've spoken about this with the Defence and I'd ask if I could do so before the cross-examination begins.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. And what is that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's the diagram. It's ERN 01167660.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: There's an original in multiple colours and then there is a translation attached to it, and I would ask that that be given a number and that it be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be P74, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. If I could remind you of the affirmation you took at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can I start now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We were just waiting for the shutters to go up. What will happen now is that the Defence counsel will ask you some questions. Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir, I'm over here, if you can see, and I represent Fatmir Limaj and I would like your help about a few matters, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm not getting any sound at all. Neither of these two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps if I spoke a moment, Mr. Mansfield, you might detect whether I'm on air to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You appear to be. I hope the witness is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if I am, he should be. So we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to ask you about some dates concerning the end of the war. Do you agree that the war ended in 1999 after the NATO bombing. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You said on Friday that after one year you obtained a television. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That being the case, you must have obtained a television in the year 2000. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And therefore in that year, 2000, is it right to say that sometime that year you saw Fatmir Limaj on your television set?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You saw him many times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You realised he was a well-known politician then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And if you remember, he was saying and doing good things for Kosovo at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you mention to your family anything about the man you were looking at on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only said that I think this one is Fatmir Limaj. I did not know him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But what did you tell your family about the man, Fatmir Limaj, who you were seeing on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We watched him and I remembered that he was Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I'll come to your memory in a moment, but what did you tell your family about this man on television regularly called Fatmir Limaj? What did you tell them about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them, This is the one that released me from the Lapusnik prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right. Now, that's in the year 2000. In 2001, that's the next year, this man, Fatmir Limaj, was still appearing regularly on television, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want to come to the year 2002. Do you remember in that year you were seen twice,as you said on Friday, by investigators; once in January and again in November of 2002. Do you remember those occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to speak the truth, I can't remember very well. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, you acknowledged to the Prosecutor on Friday the person you have met before giving evidence a number of times, that you had made two statements, one in January and one in November. Is it you just don't remember doing it or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have made statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: By 2002, according to you, you had a clear recollection of the man you say who had saved you and may be the reason you are here today, didn't you, according to you. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And I want to suggest to you now so that it's clear that so far as your recollection is concerned you have made a serious mistake about Fatmir Limaj. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. When you came to see the first investigator -- do you remember him, the one that saw you in January of 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember him, because there have been several people. Once I met with one person and another time I met with somebody else. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: This person, this investigator, spent far longer in your presence than the man you say is Fatmir Limaj, didn't he? The investigator in January, he spent -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's how it was. Do you remember anything about this first investigator from the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You can't? You can't even give a description of him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's been a long time, seven years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I've said the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It was a long time between your release, you say, and the first time in 2002. That was nearly four years, wasn't it, on this first occasion when you were being seen in 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you were talking about, or being asked to remember back four years in 2002, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's not easy, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did this first investigator tell you why he wanted to speak to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wanted me to describe the truth. He wanted to know the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did he mention any names to you? Don't say what the names are, for the moment. Did he mention any names to you of people he was interested in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did he mention any names of people who he described as suspects?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He mentioned some, but it's been a long time and we suffered these traumas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. May I say at once: I don't wish to take you back through your traumas at all. That is understandable. I would like your help about whether this investigator mentioned the names of suspects that he was interested in to see if you could help him. Did he mention any names of suspects?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The key question I want to ask you about is this: Did you tell this first investigator about Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Nothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only that he released me from prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. What do you think you told the first investigator about Fatmir Limaj besides he released you from prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing else. There is -- there was nothing else to tell him. He only released me and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: All right. Of course on your account, that's very -- that's a very important memory, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Important?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. It's a memorable event, something you would remember, you say, because he released you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to go slowly over this part of it. The suggestion I make to you is this: That you did not tell the first investigator anything about Fatmir Limaj releasing you. Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've told everybody who questioned me, I told them that Fatmir Limaj released me. There was nothing else to tell them, but I told them that he released me from prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I want to suggest you did no such thing and that what you have done is over time you have put the person you saw on television back into the situation when he wasn't there to release you in the first place. Now, is there any possibility you've done that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw him on TV. And the person I saw on TV was the one that released me from prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I want you to look at a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've had the document itself circulated. And there are copies of it, but I can give a reference for it if it's possible to put it on screen. It's 0323, the number, 1239. I don't need it on the witness's screen for -- unless he wants to have it there. It's just so Your Honours can follow the point I'm about to make. For the benefit of the witness: This is a statement, copy of a statement, the first statement you made in January 2002, to an investigator whose name appears on it. And you have signed this statement. This is in English. There is an Albanian version of this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to put to you, sir, the one sentence in this statement which relates to Fatmir Limaj. And I'm going to read it twice so you may understand what you dictated to somebody and what that person wrote down in Albanian. This is what you wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's in the middle of the second page, 1240, at the end of the main paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: "After this" -- that is, after Fehmi had died -- "After this I remember one day that a UCK soldier opened the door and looked" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, it should read "in."

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: "He did not say anything. One of the prisoners said it was Fatmir Limaj." I'll read it once again so you have it clearly. "After this" -- the death of Fehmi, namely -- "I remember one day that a UCK soldier opened the door and looked in. He did not say anything. One of the prisoners said it was Fatmir Limaj."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. Fatmir Limaj released me from there and Shala opened the door. Shala knows that. I did not see Fatmir Limaj anymore there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: If your account to the Tribunal on Friday and today is correct, this account in this statement is totally wrong, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, let's go through it. It's very short. First of all, you do not suggest that the person who came to the door was a UCK commander or that you understood that he was, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You go on to say in the statement that this soldier "did not say anything." On your account you saw him twice and he certainly spoke to you on both occasions. So that's wrong, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you understand these questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand them well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, if you understand them well, you told the investigator that the man you understood to be Fatmir Limaj did not say anything.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator when I went -- when I was in Pristina, maybe they had a Serb over there or maybe they wrote it wrongly. I don't know what they've written there. Because Fatmir Limaj just released me from there and I haven't seen him -- I did not see him anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Please understand. We know what you are claiming Fatmir Limaj said in your case. The point is, you did not claim that to the first investigator; did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said them to him, but there was a Serbian interpreter and translator, and I did not know him. And they have made mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did they read this statement over to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that day they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That day they didn't. But there came -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But there certainly did come a time when you were asked to go through this statement, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. That was before you made the statement in November later that year, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And you made a number of corrections to this first statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But in relation to this, that's the section after this "I remember one day a UCK soldier," you did not indicate to the second investigator that you had made a mistake about Mr. Limaj and that in fact he'd come twice to where you were and he had spoken and that therefore the first statement was wrong. You never said that to the second investigator, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't tell him that. I only told him that -- he asked me a week before that and he said that, I will take your case into consideration. And then he came back again and said, you may go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why did you not tell the second investigator that you'd made a mistake about Limaj, that in fact it was quite different? Why didn't you say you'd made a mistake about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object, Your Honour. If -- it's not clear to me which second investigator we're talking about here. But if it's the ICTY investigator, that misrepresents the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's the ICTY investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The ICTY statement clearly states that he said that Fatmir Limaj came on two occasions, as he testified here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid that's not quite the point. The statement goes through indicating where he's made mistakes in the first one and indicates in that second statement, I made a mistake about X, Y, and Z. Those are corrected. The point is he never said to Mr. Tucker that he made a mistake in his first statement about Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it became a little lost to the point, I'm afraid, to me, Mr. Mansfield, because you went on to say about him coming twice, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So if you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- make the point clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I think the witness has accepted that he didn't tell the second investigator that he'd made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You see, you told the first investigator, the one you saw in January, and I've read out the portion, that one of the prisoners said it was Fatmir Limaj. By that time in January, you say you'd seen him on television throughout 2000, or that part of it, and 2001, and that's how you knew him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, which is it? Was it a prisoner who told you or was it that you'd seen him on television?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I saw him myself on television. And it was learned Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that he was Fatmir Limaj. And I recognised him a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, then, how is it you were telling the first investigator that you knew Fatmir Limaj's name because one of the prisoners had told you? Why is that being written down by you, or at least written down at your dictation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of the prisoners told me that because we did not dare to speak to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war, I saw him on television, and I learned more or less -- and I recognised that he was Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The question is: How did the first investigator learn from you that you knew his name from one of the prisoners? How did that get written down as your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know his name and nobody else knew his name there. We did not dare to speak to each other as prisoners. But after the war, we learned that his name was Fatmir Limaj. And it was him, when he appeared on TV. Because there, we did not dare to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. I will ask it one more time only. How is it your statement to the first investigator suggests in your words in Albanian that you'd learnt the name from another prisoner? How does that statement come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there was somebody there, or maybe because of the war. It's been seven years since the war -- since the war and we've suffered traumas. But as I said, Fatmir Limaj just came there and released me. And I had no other contact with him whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I want to ask you about another incident involving another person. The incident concerns some UCK soldiers who made you walk to the house of someone else, right at the beginning of the journey that you say -- to Lapusnik. Now, do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You were made to walk to a house before you ever reached, you say, Lapusnik, you had to walk to a house and then you ended up in a car. Do you remember the walk to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember walking. That house was the house of Idriz Muharani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to rise, but if we're going to get into these sorts of questions, I suggest we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I've tried to avoid it, but it's the name of a soldier if it's of any assistance. I don't need the name, I just need the fact that he identified somebody.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think with this witness it's difficult to dance around these names and the risk of these names coming out is very high.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand your caution. I think Mr. Mansfield has been quite careful to date. I will -- I think we can take the risk a little longer. The Chamber is naturally reluctant to preclude the public hearing unless it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am going to change that, I regret, because I have just been informed of the technology that's failing. Today the delay machine has failed, so it's impossible to redact anything that is said. It's on air. For that reason, I regret for the members of the public that it is necessary to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I am asking you about the occasion when you had to wait for about an hour before some UCK soldiers came and made you walk to the house that you've already mentioned. So are you clear about the time I'm asking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Four soldiers came, not one, but four. And they took us. We walked for 500 metres to the -- on the mountain to the house where -- that you mentioned. And we went there. I asked them -- I said, Can I ask you something? They said, Yes. And I asked them, Are you Serbs or Albanians? And they said, We are Albanians [as interpreted]. And they said, Get into the car -- in the boot of the car -- into the boot of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, you say -- I want to ask you about those four soldiers. Sorry, I'm pausing in case there is a problem. There's not a problem. I want to ask you about whether you ever have been in a position to identify any of those four soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of them. They did not have masks, but I did not know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you ever tell anybody that you would be in a position to recognise one of them again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not those. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you ever tell anybody that you thought you knew the name of one of the four?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only what I heard, a little bit, Elise, Elise. But I can't recognise their faces. But a name, Elez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, in the statement dated the 19th of January, there is a passage about this. You indicated to the first investigator that you "waited for about an hour and two" -- not four, two -- "other UCK soldiers with uniforms came and made us walk 500 metres." Now, on what you're saying today, that's wrong. There were four, not two. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- we've suffered traumas. I've said the truth, and there is no need for these question because I have -- what -- I've said the truth about what I've experienced. I did not say anything about what I have not experienced. But we have suffered big traumas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You do appreciate that it is very important that you do not misidentify people in relation to these difficult events. You do realise that importance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People that I don't know, I don't know. And the people I know, I have described there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That is why I am asking you questions. May I just go on in this statement about these two soldiers. You say to the first investigator: "I did not know who these two UCK soldiers were, but I am sure I can recognise one of them today." That was in January 2002. Was that true, that you could recognise one of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: So why did you say it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I would ask that if this is going to be put to the witness, that the entire -- the following couple of sentences be read and put entirely into context. While I'm on my feet, if that's going to be done, I suggest that that be done in private session, since it's identifies places and names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we're driven to it, regrettably. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: In September 1998 you were interviewed by Serbian police. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did they keep a record as far as you could see of the interview? In other words, did they write it down as they were asking you questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They came for a fine regarding the vehicle registration card.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Now, you may not have understood. Were you not interviewed, according to you, by the Serbian police about what had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you tell the Serbian police about Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: After the war -- well, sorry, not after the war. During -- 1998, I understand it was September 1998. After you had gone back to your [inaudible] village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: That's correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me from Breg i Zi and they took me to the Lipjan police station and they started questioning me: Where are you from? I'm from this village. Where have you been? And I said, I've been imprisoned. I was exhausted. I could hardly speak. I have been in Lapusnik, I told them. Where did you keep them? And that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Was that interview or those questions, were they written down and your answers written down so far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not see anyone writing down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you mention a UCK commander who had released you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't mention any name over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When did you first reveal, in other words tell, anyone that you'd spoken to the Serbian police about your experiences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not revealed this to anyone, neither to my family, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When did you first reveal it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time it was over here, and also when I was examined in Pristina, it was during a conversation with those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Which people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones from the Tribunal. It is them who I told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Was it Mr. Tucker or was it Mr. Whiting or was it someone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember, because it's a long time since that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: What you had been telling the investigators on more than one occasion was that you had never reported this matter or spoken about it to anyone outside your family. That's what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I have stated, and I have never discussed it, neither with my family or with anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'll make it clear. You have indicated that what had happened to you in, you say, Lapusnik had not been discussed with anyone other than your family. That is what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sorry, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Up until very recently, we don't have a date, you had been saying that no one other than your family knew about your experiences in Lapusnik. You told the investigators, No one -- I've told no one else. You had not reported it and you hadn't spoken to anyone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had not discussed it with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But you had been asked to speak with the Serbian police about it. Hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell the investigators when they took the statements from you that in fact you had spoken to the Serbian police about these matters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't think too much about it. And trust me, we were quite exhausted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of any of the three people who interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was only one person over there. He was an Albanian with them, and also Roma people and also a Serb. They questioned me over there. They were in three [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Did you think the Albanian was called Fatmir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fatmir, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to see if we can take it a bit further. What other names can you remember from the interview, the people who were with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't give any interview over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Had you seen them before or since?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not seen them anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: On Friday you indicated that you had shown them -- that's the word that's been translated, "shown them" -- Lapusnik. Did you take them to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Otherwise, I could not lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could I have the page reference for that, if I could?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Yes, it's my page 69. I gather the lines are slightly different. It's day 9, 11.26.2004, line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When did you take them to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not take them to Lapusnik. When they questioned me and asked me, Where have you been? I told them that I was in Lapusnik. I was held there in prison. And full stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, there may be problems with translation, I don't know, but I'm going on what has been translated and the witness's answer was: "Did you take them to Lapusnik? "A. Yes, I did." So that it didn't -- I'm sorry to intervene.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not dare them to take them -- dare to take them to Lapusnik. Nobody dared.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: But I want to ask you a little more about Lapusnik. You say you recognised Lapusnik because -- on Friday because you had friends there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Were the friends that you had - I don't want the names or anything, certainly not in public - but were the friends you say you had still there in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Which one? I do not understand. Which investigator?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It's the first one. Not Mr. Tucker, it's another one. I can give his name if it matters, but you say you don't know his name or don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You do not know. Did you do any drawing for the first investigator of Lapusnik itself or the farm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have done one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes. Did you do it for the first investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember whether it was the first or the second one. I know that I'd drawn a sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, it could be translation, so I'm going to go slowly again. On Friday - and it's been put into evidence so could we have it on screen, please, P74, otherwise ERN 01167660.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It has names in it, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, it better -- yes, it better be in private session then, under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to see this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in addition the monitors. If it goes up on the monitors -- either the shades drawn or not, if the assistants could avoid having them on the monitors.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Witness, we are in open session, so I'd just remind you to be careful about mentioning names. Let me repeat the question. When the man you have identified as Fatmir Limaj told you at Lapusnik that you would be released, what was your reaction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I say? When he told me, You will go home, I was startled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And are you certain, sir, as you sit here today that that man was Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And when you were interviewed by the ICTY in November of 2002, did you tell the ICTY investigator about -- that Fatmir Limaj was the one who released you or ordered you released from Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wrote this, that he released me from prison. Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You were asked quite a few questions about your interview with CCIU/UNMIK in January 2002. Do you remember all those questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the questions. A long time has passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: No, I mean you remember being asked about that today by the Defence counsel, about your interview with CCIU/UNMIK.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they asked me, but I know that I have written the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: The interview that you had with CCIU/UNMIK, do you remember about how long that interview lasted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One hour and a half, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And where did the interview take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You said that before the interview, some people came to your house to tell you to come to the interview.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When those people came to the house, how long did you speak with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long; ten, 15 minutes maybe. That's it. They took notes, and then they summoned me afterwards. And then I went to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When you had the interview in Pristina with CCIU/UNMIK, you spoke several times about the interpreter. Do you know if the interpreter was a Serb or an Albanian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but they spoke a different language. We didn't understand what they were talking about. So maybe they have made -- have written differently what we have told them. They were Serbs. What do I know?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You had difficulty understanding the interpreter? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And did you have any difficulty trusting the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She -- there was an American lady. She knew the language very well. Because the others I didn't trust. But this lady, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: When did you see the American lady? Was that when you were interviewed by the CCIU/UNMIK or by the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about something else, sir. After you left Lapusnik, left the prison in Lapusnik and were -- and marched with the other prisoners to Berisa, after that, have you ever returned to that place that was the prison? Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was impossible to go there again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Sir, you described the room that you were in for nearly two months in Lapusnik, and you described that there was a window in that room.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only one, a small one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Could light come into that window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little light, very little, because there was also a wooden plank in front of the window, so it prevented the light from entering the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: You were asked some questions about your ability to see Shala. Can you tell the Court again, how often did you see Shala? Was it every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day, every morning in the -- in midday and sometimes he opened the door and asked us, How do you feel? And he let us go out. For as long as I was there, he was there too. He became like a family member to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And when he brought food, would he come into the room you were in to bring you the food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: And when you marched with the other prisoners to Berisa on that last day, was that during the day or was that at nighttime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day, the daytime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: During the nearly two months that you were in Lapusnik and during that final day when you marched to Berisa, did you have a clear view of Shala's face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-06 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him very well. When we were climbing this mountain, Shala told us to get ourselves by the hand. And he said, if one of you lets go of the hand, I will kill him. I was the last in the line. Shala was behind me. Murrizi was in front. And this is how we marched up the mountains of Berisa. There is a meadow there, surrounded by two mountains, and this is where we stopped for some two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If I could just have one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sir, I am able to tell you that that is the end of the questions you will be asked. You will now be able to go back to your home. The Chamber wishes to thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance you have given us. After we adjourn now, you will be free to go and you will be given advice about how you will go home. Mr. Whiting, we will take the break now and resume at 25 minutes to. Is that convenient with the next witness? Am I looking at the right person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I can answer the person. Mr. Cayley will have the next witness, and that is convenient, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 25 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I am now going to ask you to make an affirmation. Would you please repeat after me. I solemnly declare.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That I will speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I will speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The whole truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Mr. Cayley will now ask you some questions. Yes, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honour, if I may identify the witness. And if the usher could -- could you just whisper his name in his ear and ask if that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness, you need to speak up a little bit. Is that your name that's just been read to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could show it to the Defence, please, and also to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Exhibit Number will be P75, under seal, for this pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And my understanding is, Your Honour, this witness will be L-04. I'll proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness, I realise that giving evidence is something you've never done before, and I can understand you're feeling a little nervous. Relax as best you can. Speak slowly. Listen very carefully to the questions that I ask you, and only address matters that I raise in my question. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, if we could go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Witness, after this beating, can you tell the Judges what happened to you next.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes, after they beat us they took us by our arms, Alush Gashi, and he put us in a combi van.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: (redacted) There were only seats in the front. We were lying in the boot. There was nothing there, no seats. I was behind the driver while my cousin was on the other side, next to me. And we went along the road. I was trying to figure out which way we were going. I knew the road very well. I had been there before the war. I had gone along that road before the war. The car was driving on the left. The car kept left. And I found myself in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you can recall, how long did the journey take from receiving your beating to finding yourself in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: I don't know what to say. It was -- the car followed various roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You can't recall how long the journey took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: An hour maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you say that you found yourself in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, on the journey from your beating to arriving in Lapusnik, you had a sack on your head. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes. Both of us had sacks on our heads. But I was trying to figure out which way we were going. I couldn't see, but I knew the road. There is an asphalted road where a village called Sedlare is. There is a little bit of asphalted road there. Well, the road goes to the right, but our car went, turned left. And that's how I knew that I was in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, when you got to Lapusnik, can you tell the Judges what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes. When we got to Lapusnik, they got us out of the car and they put us in. Shala took the sacks off our heads, both of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Did you know that the individual that took the sacks off your heads at that time was called Shala?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes. I had heard. I heard from a soldier. A soldier said, Shala, please, open the door. Get these. And he was a guard, sort of a guard there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So when you arrived you heard a soldier address an individual as Shala. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at Lapusnik, was it dark or light? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: It was morning, around 10.00, probably half past 10.00 at most.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And it was summertime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: Yes. It was June.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What did Shala tell you and your relative to do, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L-04
utterances.text: When we got in there Shala searched everything we had in our pockets and also on [Realtime transcript read in error: "in"] our wrists. He wanted us to hand them over to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can go into private session now because I think there's a risk of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on the 30th day of November, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
